We can estimate decimal division by rounding each decimal to the nearest whole number and dividing the resulting numbers.

Content:
For example, suppose we wish to estimate the quotient of the following division problem.
[MATH: 19.7 \div 5.3]

One way to proceed is first to round both quantities to the nearest whole number:

Content:
[MATH: 19.7|÷|5.3; ↓|↓; 20|÷|5]

Content:
So, we can form an estimate of [MATH: 19.7 \div 5.3] by evaluating [MATH: 20 \div 5.]

Content:
Computing the quotient of this simplified problem gives

Content:
[MATH: 20 \div 5 = 4.]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 19.7 \div 5.3] is approximately equal to [MATH: 4.] We can write this symbolically as follows:
[MATH: 19.7 \div 5.3 \approx 4]

Content:
The symbol [MATH: \approx] means "is approximately equal to."

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can estimate decimal division by rounding each decimal to the nearest whole number and dividing the resulting numbers.

Computing the quotient of this simplified problem gives

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 19.7 \div 5.3] is approximately equal to [MATH: 4.] We can write this symbolically as follows:
[MATH: 19.7 \div 5.3 \approx 4]
